title: Synthesis cache ignores the lens: a lens change silently reuses old LLM outputs
description: Found 2026-09-02 while running the berd validation. Both tricorder-synthesize.py (legacy, <cache>/synthesis/) and learn (v2, .raw/synthesis/) cache Phase 1-4 outputs keyed only by PR number, reviewer, author. Switching lenses on a warm cache reuses outputs produced under the previous lens's prompts and category enum, so a desktop-lens run would report dbt-lens results. The berd validation only avoided this because the old synthesis dir was moved aside by hand. Fix: key the cache directory by lens name and version (synthesis/<lens>-v<version>/), record the lens in each cached file, and refuse to load a cached entry whose lens differs. Keep the default behaviour of resuming within the same lens.
acceptance_criteria: Running synthesize with --lens A then --lens B on the same cache produces two synthesis dirs and B's phase outputs contain none of A's categories; a unit test covers the cache key.
close_reason: Fixed on fix/lens-keyed-cache: tricorder/lenses/cache.py keys synthesis dirs by lens name+version, stamps every cached file, refuses cross-lens entries, migrates flat layouts; wired into synthesize, learn, and the renderer; 6 unit tests.

title: Oversight density: approvals without engagement, per reviewer and per file tag
description: Framing (Dave, 2026-09-02): in agentic development, code review is where human oversight concentrates, so the review record is the audit trail of human judgment over machine-generated change. The failure to detect is rubber-stamping, not a reviewer blind spot. Metric, computed in Phase 4 from data already harvested (no LLM): per reviewer, PRs reviewed, approvals, silent approvals (approve with no body and no inline comment), inline comments per reviewed PR; per lens file tag, comment count, distinct reviewers, and share of PRs touching the tag with zero human comment. Per-axis needs the changed-files list per PR, which the legacy harvest does not store (comments carry paths; file lists do not exist) — extend harvest/analyze to record changed files. Author-type split (human vs agent-assisted PRs) needs an author classifier; berd is the test case because its record is mostly humans reviewing agent-assisted work. Prototype: scratchpad tricorder-oversight.py run on the berd cache 2026-09-02.
acceptance_criteria: learnings.json carries oversight: {per_reviewer, per_tag} for berd; explorer shows silent-approval share on Reviewer Fingerprints; a tag with >=5 PRs and zero comments is reported as an oversight gap in Phase 4.
close_reason: Implemented on feat/oversight-density: harvest and analyze record changed files (with backfill); tricorder/oversight.py computes per-reviewer silent approvals and per-axis silent share via new axis->file-tag mappings in the desktop lens; written to oversight.json, fed to Phase 4, shown on Team Gaps and Reviewer Fingerprints. berd 2026-09-03: 65/163 PRs no human engagement; capability-minimality 11/11 and webview-csp 10/10 touching PRs silent; packaging 39/40; updater 35/36; dependencies 33/34. telemetry-privacy has no path mapping and is not measurable this way.

title: Decision: never composite lenses; abstain below min_score, report mixed below min_margin
description: Per findings Q6. No published classifier exposes a threshold for this problem, so thresholds are a design choice to calibrate empirically. Rules: (1) score after applying the global ignore list; (2) below min_score report unknown and run no lens; (3) top-two margin below min_margin means mixed: attach the runner-up's axes as a secondary Phase 4 section, do not blend authority lists; (4) per-path nuance lives in file_tags, not merged rubrics; (5) composition_check and review_path_check must both pass before synthesis spends money.

title: Decision: product-engineering is a parent with sub-profiles (desktop, mobile, backend-service, library, cli)
description: Per findings Q2 (Backstage's small-core/open-extension taxonomy). Keep the five top-level archetypes; add sub-profiles under product-engineering via the lens 'extends' field. Archetype describes the artifact being engineered, not what it does: berd's subject is AI agents but its code archetype is a desktop app. Consequence: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md/.agents never count as archetype evidence.

description: Synthesis change 4. Current: runner-up axes go to Phase 4 as a secondary section reported only with evidence. On berd bb-cli/ is 5.5%, so no secondary.

title: Decision: security and agent-engineering as overlays, not top-level archetypes
description: Synthesis change 3. Claude pass: no published taxonomy (Backstage, crates.io, PyPI, Borges et al. 2016) has security or agent-engineering as an artifact kind; they describe what an artifact does. Tricorder already has security as a --focus-on area, and after the ignore list the security lens rarely wins detection. Proposal: overlays that add categories, axes, authorities and must_not on top of a primary artifact lens; detection never selects them as primary.
